name: nlp_sklearn_text_leaky
title: The classic TF-IDF + LogisticRegression sentiment baseline, leaking in three places
origin: hardening round 1, domain-nlp, 2026-09-13 - the defective twin of nlp_sklearn_text_pipeline
note: MLV305 and MLV306 miss for one shared reason: report() receives the fitted search as a parameter, so grid.decision_function() and grid.predict() resolve to nothing and their outputs carry no LOGITS / PREDS tag. Binding the estimator in the same scope makes both fire (finding NLP-03).

expected.defect: the TF-IDF vocabulary and idf weights are fitted on every review, one line before the split
expected.why: the held-out reviews decide which 50 000 n-grams get a column and what each one's inverse document frequency is, so the reported test score is optimistic by a margin nobody can estimate

expected.defect: the feature split takes no random_state
expected.why: the reported accuracy moves between runs by more than most of the differences this grid search is trying to measure

expected.defect: the text split takes no random_state either
expected.why: as well as being irreproducible, this second unseeded draw is what makes test_x and test_y describe different rows

expected.defect: a second TfidfVectorizer is fitted on the held-out reviews so that rare words in them get their own columns
expected.why: the model is scored on a matrix whose columns mean something different from the ones it was trained on, and the vocabulary it is scored with was learned from the answers

expected.defect: the grid search is handed a bare LogisticRegression and an already-vectorised matrix
expected.why: all five folds share one vocabulary and one set of idf weights, so the cross-validated score that picks C is itself optimistic

expected.defect: accuracy_score is handed grid.decision_function() output rather than grid.predict()
expected.why: it compares signed margins with 0/1 labels, so the accuracy printed is near the chance rate whatever the model does

expected.defect: the ROC AUC is computed over predict() output, which is hard 0/1 labels
expected.why: AUC over two points is balanced accuracy wearing an AUC label, and it hides exactly the threshold behaviour AUC exists to show - especially odd here, where decision_function() was already computed three lines above

expected.defect: nothing seeds numpy or random and no estimator takes random_state
expected.why: neither split, nor the liblinear solver's tie-breaking, nor the grid search's fold assignment can be repeated

forbidden.why: there is no torch training loop in this project at all
there is no DataLoader in this project
there is no torch module and no evaluation loop; scoring is one call to predict()
a review corpus carries no temporal signal - no to_datetime, no parse_dates, no date-named column, no statsmodels import - so a random split is the right split here
line 34 is MLV102's finding, not MLV101's: extra is fitted on the held-out half, not before the split, and stacking both codes on one fit site would be two findings for one root cause
no Keras model appears in this project

unsupported.defect: the second split draws a different random permutation from the first, so test_x (rebuilt from test_text on line 34) and test_y (from line 30) describe different reviews; every reported number is a comparison of unrelated rows
unsupported.why: no rule relates two split calls over the same frame; MLView reports each one's missing random_state independently and nothing checks that two splits of the same data agree

unsupported.defect: a derived column is added to the frame and never used, which is harmless here but is the shape that becomes target leakage the moment the derivation touches the label
unsupported.why: MLV105 (target column left inside the feature matrix) is a later-tier rule and is not built
